tones.title: Marantz SD 3020 tape deck - cassette player (1979) - 1000 epochs
tones.description:
The Marantz 3020 is a vintage solid-state integrated amplifier celebrated for its warm, musical character and understated power. Released in the late 1970s, it embodied Marantz’s approach to hi-fi: clean circuitry, reliable build quality, and a tonal signature that leaned smooth and inviting rather than clinical. Its preamp section in particular earned a cult following among cassette enthusiasts who valued depth, clarity, and a touch of analog sweetness.

It has been my number one machine for making mixtapes and tape duplicates at normal and high speed thanks to its stable output and forgiving yet detailed sound. I also love running microphones into it to record acoustic guitar because it captures transients and harmonics in a way that feels intimate without ever becoming sharp or brittle.

This NAM capture was made direct using a tube preamp equipped with a NOS Brimar 12AU7 / ECC82 WA tube, adding extra harmonic texture. The resulting tone is dark and rich, excelling beautifully in the mid and high ranges.

a2_models.name: Marantz SD 3020 tape deck - vintage cassette player

tones.title: Ampeg B-18N Portaflex Fliptop
tones.description:
1964 Ampeg B18N - The big brother to the legendary B-15N, delivering 50 watts of vintage tube bass tone through the same beloved B15 preamp circuit. This rare Portaflex head represents Ampeg's push for more power while maintaining that warm, pillowy low-end and musical midrange compression that defined the era's bass sound.

Amp head captured at three gain stages from clean to driven saturation using a Suhr Reactive Load Box.

Note: This is an amp-only capture - pair with your favorite bass cab IR for the full experience. Works beautifully with vintage 15" or 18" speaker IRs to recreate that authentic tone.

tones.title: Philips EL3541D Tape player Mic input
tones.description:
Capture of an old tube driven tape recorder and player from Philips.
I chose the very gainy mic input, which leads to produce a very gnarly fuzz when driven too hard.
Since I took the signal from the speaker out, power amp is captured aswell. this is the internal amplifiers only though, so son't expect any tape saturation.
(The tape is too warbly, signal not coherent enough for the ML process)

Signal chain: Interface -> Reamp box -> Mic input tape recorder -> speaker out -> Load box -> Interface.

tones.title: CAPI VP28 Preamp - 19dBu Send/Return - TTSV10
tones.description:
I've uploaded updated captures of one of my CAPI VP28 500-series microphone preamps in Line Mode. The preamp is based on the circuitry in an API console. 

The signal passes through 3 transformers and 2 op amps. The concept is that it has an API 312 preamp (input transformer, discrete op amp, output transformer) and an adaptation of console fader circuitry (op amp, transformer).

The preamp is configured with GAR2520 and GAR1731 op amps in the Preamp and Fader positions respectively.

I used my RME UCX II interface set at 19dBu on the send and return. 

I used the rotary switches of the Preamp and Fader controls to achieve nominal unity gain (eg. +12dB Preamp and -12dB Fader).

I recommend setting NAM to the Raw output mode. The intent is that you are essentially running your signal through my hardware insert. You can drive the input for more saturation if desired.

Turn off the Gate for the full signal to come through.

I originally uploaded low ESR Standard Architecture captures. I decided to also train some xSTD captures to see if it makes any difference.

tones.title: AMPEG SVT-CL BASS HEAD
tones.description:
Ampeg SVT-CL – Bass Preamp Capture

Epochs: 1000 | Reamp Box: Countryman 85

⚠️Disclaimer: The online preview player does not accurately represent these captures. For the best tone and true-to-source results, please download the files and use them within the NAM plugin alongside a high-quality impulse response at the correct input gain.

Plug into the undisputed king of bass amplification with the Ampeg SVT-CL — captured to deliver the massive low end, punchy mids, and unmistakable tones that have powered countless legendary recordings and live rigs.

This profile delivers the classic SVT growl, depth and clarity: thick, weighty lows that stay tight, thick midrange punch for perfect mix placement, and a smooth yet present top end that preserves attack and articulation. Ideal for rock, metal, punk, and modern bass production where power and definition must coexist, mixed with some Sansamp and Darkglass for good measure!

Please Note: This is a preamp-only capture — no cabinet IR is included, giving you complete freedom to pair with your preferred bass cab IRs or power amp simulations.
